items.title: Jayson Tatum’s soft technical foul cost the Celtics the game, and it was completely avoidable
items.summary: The Boston Celtics had one last chance to tie the game against the Denver Nuggets on Wednesday night, trailing by three with six seconds remaining. Jamal Murray had just extended Denver’s lead with a tough mid-range pull-up, and the Celtics called timeout after the ball swished through the net. As his team was walking to the huddle, Boston star Jayson Tatum threw the ball towards the official at center court. He was given a technical foul, and it ultimately cost his team the game.The Nuggets beat the Celtics, 105-101, after the controversial technical was given to Tatum. The ESPN broadcasters agreed that Tatum deserved the technical, but fans online are still fuming after what they perceive as another soft tech for Tatum. Tatum could have just handed the ball to the official next to him. Instead, he threw it in frustration to the official at halfcourt who wasn’t looking for the ball.…

items.title: Kawhi Leonard Dealing With Patellar Tendinopathy
items.summary: The Raptors’ headline offseason acquisition, Kawhi Leonard only played two games for his new team this season before being sidelined with what was described as left knee swelling. Nearly four weeks into Leonard’s absence, Josh Lewenberg reports for TSN Sports (Twitter video link) that the star forward is actually dealing with patellar tendinopathy. That’s the same recurring condition that Leonard and Toronto were forced to manage in his previous stint with the Raptors in 2019, which required significant load management. The nature of the condition, which is a result of areas within the quadriceps tendon developing some level of degeneration, is such that it can only be effectively treated by reducing high-stress activity, Lewenberg notes. That has led the team to be more cautious when it comes to Leonard’s return timeline. The two-time NBA Finals MVP is still progressing in his return…

items.title: Players Eligible For In-Season Veteran Extensions In 2026/27
items.summary: As we explain in our glossary entry on veteran contract extensions, rookie scale extensions used to be the most common form of contract extension in the NBA. However, recent Collective Bargaining Agreements have loosened the rules on eligibility for veteran extensions and made them more financially advantageous, especially for players who don’t expect mega-deals. As a result, we’ve seen a substantial bump in veteran contract extensions in recent seasons. In every league year since 2021/22, at least 17 players have signed veteran extensions, including 20 in 2025/26. We’re not quite up to 17 yet in ’26/27, but there’s plenty of time for this season’s list to continue to grow, right up until June 30, 2027.
